paragraphs: Friend, look at who is laughing in this passage. The Philistines are praising Dagon, a false god, and saying their god delivered Samson into their hands (Judges 16:23). Samson is blind, hauled out of a prison, and stationed between two pillars to entertain them. It looks like the end of the road for him, and I'd say the crowd thought so too.

But look at what Samson does in the dark. He doesn't call out to the crowd. He calls out to the LORD: "O Lord GOD, please remember me" (Judges 16:28). That's the heart of this whole passage. He had a long road of bad choices behind him, and still he turned to God and asked. I know what it's like to be stuck in the dark thinking nobody's coming, so this part gets me every time.

And the passage doesn't hide how this ends. Samson dies with the Philistines, and in his death he killed more than he had killed in his life (Judges 16:30). I think this one is heavy, and I'll just say that plainly. Still, the last word isn't the Philistines' party. It's that Samson had judged Israel twenty years (Judges 16:31), and God was still working through a worn-out man who asked Him for help. So when you feel used up, baker, ask Him anyway. This is the end of Samson's story, but the One he called on is still listening.
